correctness.rationale: The diffusion matrix is a sum of three rank-one outer products whose fifth and sixth entries vanish identically, so \(e_5\) and \(e_6\) are exact kernel vectors and uniform positive definiteness is impossible. The displayed Lyapunov function has no \(x_5\) dependence, giving \(V(x^*+t e_5)=0\) on an unbounded positive ray. Eq. (50) has no \(x_3\) or \(x_5\) term, and an explicit family with either coordinate arbitrarily large remains on the level set. These direct algebraic checks require no numerical approximation and are replayed by verify.py.

originality.rationale: The general fact that a seven-dimensional diffusion driven by three Brownian motions has rank at most three, and the fact that degenerate epidemic diffusions need special ergodic arguments, are known. What is new here is the source-specific implication comparison: system (4) has exact kernel directions \(e_5\) and \(e_6\) that make the article's own Lemma 3.3 ellipticity condition impossible, while Theorem 4.2 simultaneously uses a Lyapunov function omitting \(x_5\) and an Eq. (50) level set omitting \(x_3\) and \(x_5\). Exact source/title/DOI and alias searches found no correction or publication stating these three linked defects.

value.rationale: The defect sits in the paper's main unique-stationary-distribution/ergodicity theorem, not in an ancillary calculation. Uniform ellipticity versus degenerate diffusion determines which ergodic machinery is available, while failure of coercivity invalidates the bounded recurrent-set construction as written. A repair would require a genuinely new degenerate-diffusion argument or a materially different Lyapunov/support analysis, so the finding has structural value beyond notation checking.
